news.title: VARROC: Softer Margins And Revenue Assumptions Will Cap Future Upside
news.body: Analysts have trimmed their price target on Varroc Engineering from ₹550 to ₹520, reflecting updated views on slightly softer revenue growth, profit margin assumptions, and a marginally higher discount rate, while keeping long term P/E expectations broadly unchanged. What's in the News Varroc Engineering has announced an annual dividend of ₹1.50 per share, with payment scheduled for September 19, 2026, and the ex date and record date on August 7, 2026.

news.title: Dividend increased to ₹1.50
news.body: Dividend of ₹1.50 is 50% higher than last year. Ex-date: 7th August 2026 Payment date: 19th September 2026 Dividend yield will be 0.3%, which is lower than the industry average of 0.6%. Sustainability & Growth Dividend is well covered by both earnings (25% earnings payout ratio) and cash flows (22% cash payout ratio). The dividend has decreased over the past 76 years, indicating a lack of growth and stability in payments. EPS is expected to grow by 141% over the next 3 years, which should provide support to the dividend and adequate earnings cover.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: EPS misses analyst expectations
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: ₹0.67 loss per share (improved from ₹3.10 loss in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹22.9b (up 10% from 3Q 2025). Net loss: ₹103.0m (loss narrowed 78% from 3Q 2025). Revenue was in line with analyst estimates. Earnings per share (EPS) missed analyst estimates. Revenue is forecast to grow 11% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 11% growth forecast for the Auto Components industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 7% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 28% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.

What's in the News Board meeting scheduled for Feb 5, 2026 to consider and approve unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and nine months ended Dec 31, 2025, along with other business matters (Board Meeting).

news.title: VARROC: New EV Electronics Win Will Likely Support But Not Transform Fair Pricing
news.body: Analysts have kept their fair value estimate for Varroc Engineering steady at ₹550.0 per share, with small tweaks to assumptions around the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E helping to fine tune their price target rather than shift it in a new direction. What's in the News Varroc announced a new business win with an electric vehicle OEM to supply High Voltage electronics for e-powertrain components, including power electronics units, inverters, onboard chargers, battery management systems and DC-DC converters, with peak annual capacity planned at ₹8,000 million over an 8 year delivery period (Key Developments).
